entries.description:
A function held as a value — what `Function(x) { return x * 2; }` or `Procedure(x) { … }` produces when it is written where a value is expected. TypeOf answers Function. It is called through the variable that holds it, `f(4)`, with the arguments its parameter list declares; a Procedure value answers nothing.

It keeps the variables it names from the place it was written and reads them when it is called — guide.lambda says what a lambda is for and when a clause says the same thing shorter. It has no members. It lives as long as the session that made it: it cannot be stored in the base, serialized, or handed to a background job or to another session.
entries.syntax_block:
f = Function(x) { return x * 2; };
Value = f(4);   // 8
entries.parameters: As its own parameter list declares.
entries.return_descr: What its body returns; a Procedure value answers Undefined.

entries.description: The cursor a Foreach loop walks a collection with — one per loop, kept in a hidden slot of the procedure and moved on every turn. A script never names or creates one, and it has no members; it shows among the locals in the debugger while a loop runs. Everything Foreach can walk — an Array, a Table, a Map, a LINQ query, a data source of Data — hands the loop one of these.

What a chain of LINQ verbs answers with: `arr.Where(f)`, `rows.OrderBy(k).Take(10)`, `sales.GroupBy(k)`. It holds the steps, not the rows — nothing is read until a terminal verb (Count, ToArray, First, Sum, …) or a Foreach asks for elements, and asking again walks the source again, so a query kept in a variable sees the source as it is at that moment.

Every collection Foreach can walk takes the same verbs — an Array, a Table, a ValueList, a Map, a group's Values, a data source of Data — and every verb that keeps the chain going answers with a new LinqQuery, so the verbs follow one another. ToArray turns the query into an Array, ToTable into a Table.

The query block — `from x in arr where … select …` — says the same with keywords and answers at once, with a Table; guide.linq gives both forms and the order of the clauses.
Keeps the elements predicate answers True for, in their order. A comparison with NULL inside the predicate is neither true nor false, and the element is dropped — as the WHERE of a query drops it.
entries.parameters: predicate — fn(element) answering a Boolean.

entries.description: Turns every element into what projection answers for it — one out for one in, in the same order. A row with named fields is a Structure returned from projection, or the query block's `select { A = …, B = … }`, which answers with a Table.
entries.parameters: projection — fn(element) answering the new element.

entries.description: How many elements the query yields. A collection that knows its size answers at once; a filtered sequence is walked to the end. It takes no condition — filter with Where first.
entries.parameters: None.

entries.description: Walks the query and answers with an Array of its elements, in order. This is where a query stops being steps and becomes values: the Array stays as it is when the source changes afterwards.
entries.parameters: None.

entries.description: The first element, reading no further than it. Over an empty sequence it answers Undefined — the same as FirstOrDefault; Single and Last are the verbs that raise on nothing.
entries.parameters: None.

entries.description: True when the query yields at least one element; the walk stops at the first. It takes no condition — filter with Where first. The cheap way to ask "is there one" before a total or an average.
entries.parameters: None.

entries.description: Lets each value through the first time it appears, in the order of first appearance. Values are compared the way sorting compares them.
entries.parameters: None.

entries.description: The elements in ascending order of key(element). The whole source is read before the first element comes out. The order is stable — elements with equal keys keep the order they had — so an order by two keys is two calls, the second key first: `.OrderBy(byDate).OrderBy(byItem)` orders by item, and by date within an item. The query block says it shorter: `orderby x.Item, x.Date`.
entries.parameters: key — fn(element) answering the value to order by.

entries.description: The elements in descending order of key(element) — largest first. Stable, as OrderBy is: elements with equal keys keep the order they had.
entries.parameters: key — fn(element) answering the value to order by.

entries.description: One group per distinct key(element), in the order the keys first appear. Each element of the answer is a LinqGroup: its Key, and its Values — the elements under the key, which take every verb themselves (`g.Values.Count()`, `g.Values.Sum(f)`).
entries.parameters: key — fn(element) answering the value to group by.

entries.signature: Join(inner, leftKey : Function, rightKey : Function, projection : Function) : LinqQuery
entries.description: An inner join of this sequence with inner: for every element whose leftKey(element) equals rightKey(i) of an element i of inner, projection(element, i) is yielded — one result per matching pair, in this sequence's order; an element with no match yields nothing. inner is read once and kept in memory, keyed. When both sides are data sources of Data, the join is run by the server instead.
entries.syntax_block:
Q = Outer.Join(Inner, Function(o) { return o.Key; }, Function(i) { return i.Key; },
               Function(o, i) { return <row>; });
entries.parameters:
inner — any collection Foreach can walk.
leftKey — fn(element) of this sequence.
rightKey — fn(element) of inner.
projection — fn(element, innerElement) answering the result.
entries.example:
Pairs = Orders.Join(Clients,
    Function(o) { return o.Client; },
    Function(c) { return c.Code; },
    Function(o, c) { return New Structure("Number, Name", o.Number, c.Name); }).ToArray();

entries.description: Passes over the first n elements and yields the rest. n of 0 or less skips nothing.
entries.parameters: n — how many elements to pass over.

entries.description: Yields at most the first n elements and stops reading the source there. n of 0 or less yields nothing.
entries.parameters: n — the most elements to yield.

entries.description: Passes over elements while predicate answers True. From the first element it answers False for, that element and everything after it are yielded, and predicate is not asked again.
entries.parameters: predicate — fn(element) answering a Boolean.

entries.description: Yields elements while predicate answers True and stops at the first one it answers False for — that one and the rest are not yielded, and the source is not read further.
entries.parameters: predicate — fn(element) answering a Boolean.

entries.description: The elements in the opposite order. The whole source is read before the first element comes out.
entries.parameters: None.

entries.description: This sequence's elements, then other's, duplicates kept. other is any collection Foreach can walk; a value that cannot be walked raises.
entries.parameters: other — the collection that follows.

entries.description: Concat followed by Distinct: the elements of both, each value once, in the order of first appearance.
entries.parameters: other — any collection Foreach can walk.

entries.description: The elements of this sequence that other holds too — each value once, in this sequence's order. other is read once, before the first element comes out.
entries.parameters: other — any collection Foreach can walk.

entries.description: The elements of this sequence that other does not hold — each value once, in this sequence's order. other is read once, before the first element comes out.
entries.parameters: other — any collection Foreach can walk.

entries.description: The last element; the whole sequence is read to find it. An empty sequence raises — LastOrDefault answers Undefined instead.
entries.parameters: None.

entries.description: The last element, or Undefined when the sequence is empty. The whole sequence is read.
entries.parameters: None.

entries.description: The only element. Raises when the sequence is empty and when it holds more than one — the verb for a lookup that must find exactly one. The walk stops at the second element.
entries.parameters: None.

entries.description: The only element, or Undefined when there is none; raises when there are two or more.
entries.parameters: None.

entries.description: The first element, or Undefined when the sequence is empty; nothing after the first is read.
entries.parameters: None.

entries.description: The element at index, counting from 0. A negative index, or one past the last element, raises.
entries.parameters: index — the position, from 0.

entries.description: The element at index, counting from 0, or Undefined when the index is negative or past the last element.
entries.parameters: index — the position, from 0.

entries.description: True when an element equals value; the walk stops at the first one that does.
entries.parameters: value — what an element must equal.

entries.description: True when other yields the same elements, in the same order, and as many of them. The walk stops at the first difference.
entries.parameters: other — any collection Foreach can walk.

entries.description: Folds the sequence into one value: starting from seed, reducer(accumulated, element) is called for every element in turn, and what it answers is carried to the next. An empty sequence answers seed.
entries.syntax_block: Value = Q.Aggregate(seed, Function(acc, x) { return <next acc>; });
entries.parameters:
seed — the value to start from.
reducer — fn(accumulated, element) answering the next accumulated value.
entries.example: List = Names.Aggregate("", Function(acc, n) { return ?(acc = "", n, acc + ", " + n); });

entries.description: Where with the position: predicate(element, index) is asked with the element's index in this sequence, from 0, and the element is kept when it answers True.
entries.parameters: predicate — fn(element, index) answering a Boolean.

entries.description: Select with the position: every element becomes projection(element, index), the index counted in this sequence from 0.
entries.parameters: projection — fn(element, index) answering the new element.
entries.example: Numbered = Names.SelectIndexed(Function(n, i) { return String(i + 1) + ". " + n; }).ToArray();

entries.description: Walks the query and answers with a Table. The columns come from the rows: a row with fields — a Structure, a table row, an object — gives one column per field, named as the first row names them; a group gives Key and Values; plain values go into one column named Value. On a data source of Data the table is read by the server, with the source's own columns and types.
entries.parameters: None.

entries.description: Flattens: collection(element) answers a collection for every element, and its elements are yielded in turn. With result, what is yielded is result(element, inner) for each pair, so both the outer element and the inner one are in reach — what a second `from` in a query block does. An element whose collection cannot be walked contributes nothing.
entries.parameters:
collection — fn(element) answering a collection.
result — optional fn(element, innerElement) answering what is yielded.

entries.description: The total of the elements — or of selector(element) for each — added exactly, as numbers are. Over an empty sequence a query kept in a variable answers Undefined, while a chain written in one expression, `arr.Where(f).Sum()`, answers 0: ask Any() first where the difference matters.
entries.syntax_block:
Total = Q.Sum();
Total = Q.Sum(Function(x) { return x.<Field>; });
entries.parameters: selector — optional fn(element) answering the number to add.
entries.return_descr: Number, or Undefined over nothing (see above).

entries.description: The smallest element — or the smallest selector(element): the value itself, not the element it came from. Undefined over an empty sequence.
entries.syntax_block:
Least = Q.Min();
Least = Q.Min(Function(x) { return x.<Field>; });
entries.parameters: selector — optional fn(element) answering the value to compare.

entries.description: The largest element — or the largest selector(element): the value itself, not the element it came from. Undefined over an empty sequence.
entries.syntax_block:
Most = Q.Max();
Most = Q.Max(Function(x) { return x.<Field>; });
entries.parameters: selector — optional fn(element) answering the value to compare.

entries.description: The arithmetic mean of the elements — or of selector(element) — the exact total divided by the count. Over an empty sequence a query kept in a variable answers Undefined, while a chain written in one expression, `arr.Where(f).Average()`, answers 0 — as Sum does: ask Any() first where the difference matters.
entries.syntax_block:
Mean = Q.Average();
Mean = Q.Average(Function(x) { return x.<Field>; });
entries.parameters: selector — optional fn(element) answering the number to average.
entries.return_descr: Number, or Undefined over nothing (see above).

entries.description: The rows LINQ keeps while it works, and what a group's Values is: the elements under one key, lent where they lie rather than copied. It takes every verb a LinqQuery takes — `g.Values.Count()`, `g.Values.Sum(f)`, `g.Values.Where(f)` — and Foreach walks it; it has no methods of its own, and New does not make one. ToArray turns it into an Array when the rows must be kept apart from the query.

One group of a grouping — an element of what GroupBy answers, and the `g` of `group … by … into g`. Key is the value its elements share, Values the elements themselves. Both are read-only. A query block that ends in `group … by` answers with a Table of two columns, Key and Values.
The value the group's elements share — what the key function, or the `by` of the query block, answered for them. Read-only.
The elements under the key, in the order they came — a LinqRows: take Count, Sum, Where or ToArray of it, or walk it with Foreach. Read-only.

A row of a projection — what `select { A = …, B = … }` makes for every element while the query runs: its fields, by the names written and in that order, read-only. The query's answer is a Table, so a script meets the result as table rows; a LinqRow is seen in the debugger's locals while a query is at work. Two rows compare by their values, field after field.
entries.syntax_block: T = from x in Source select { A = x.<Field>, B = x.<Field> };
entries.example:
T = from l in Lines select { Item = l.Item, Total = l.Price * l.Quantity };
Message(T[0].Total);

entries.description: The field names of one `select { … }`, held once for every row of the query, so a row carries only its values. Internal: a script never reaches it and it has no members; it shows among the locals in the debugger while a query runs.

Where the system enumerations come from. Every enumeration the platform registers — TextEncoding, HTTPMethod, SortDirection, … — is a global name through it, and its values are read after a dot: `TextEncoding.UTF8`. It is never named in a script and has no members of its own; each enumeration has its own article. A configuration's own enumerations are reached through Enumerations.

Where the global functions and procedures come from — Message, Format, CurrentDate, StrLen, RunBackground and the rest: they are its members, and a script calls them without a prefix. It is never named in a script; every function has its own article under Global functions.

What the code runner adds to a script: a Message that writes into the runner's output pane, under the code. It exists only in the code runner, which runs a script without a base or a session; in the application, Message is the global procedure.
Appends text as a line to the code runner's output pane. The argument is turned into a string.
entries.parameters: text — what to write.
